sources.note: Asks whether latent CoT destroys monitorability, and finds monitorability depends more on the task and on access to internals than on whether reasoning is explicit or latent.
sources.title: Does Out-of-Sight Equal Out-of-Mind in CoT Monitorability?

sources.note: Switches to soft-embedding latent reasoning only at low-confidence steps, keeping discrete decoding elsewhere, and pushes the soft embeddings away from the top token to stop them collapsing.
sources.title: SeLaR: Selective Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

sources.note: Tests the claim that continuous chain-of-thought lets a model hold several candidate solutions at once, and finds it holds only for models trained from scratch: off-the-shelf models collapse a superposed input to a single token within a few layers, and fine-tuned latent reasoners solve the task in one forward pass and copy the answer through the latent slots.
sources.title: The Illusion of Superposition? A Principled Analysis of Latent Thinking in Language Models

sources.note: Explains why latent chain-of-thought excels at exploration but fails at computation by identifying decisional certainty as the governing variable, formalizing it as the Symbolic Index, and proving that curriculum learning is not merely helpful but necessary for training latent reasoners.
sources.title: Capabilities and Fundamental Limits of Latent Chain-of-Thought

result.definition: A chain of thought carried in continuous states rather than emitted tokens, and across 4 sources studied for both its capability limits and its monitoring cost. On capability, one source gives a formal treatment of what continuous rollouts can and cannot achieve, and another asks whether the phenomena attributed to superposition in latent thinking survive analysis -- finding continuous and discrete decoding functionally indistinguishable on off-the-shelf models, with layer-wise entropy profiles coinciding and cosine similarity 0.996 to 0.998. On monitoring, the framing question is whether out of sight equals out of mind: with no trace to read, monitoring must fall back on probing activations or verbalising the latent states, and how much monitorability those retain is the open question. One source makes the reasoning selective rather than always-latent, which is the archive's recurring finding that a fixed latent budget is wrong in both directions.
